cohort: The study included 19,089,780 women from the National Inpatient Sample dataset from 2016 to 2020 who had delivery admissions, categorized into four groups of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy or normotensive controls.
finding: Pregnant patients with chronic hypertension, preeclampsia, and chronic hypertension with superimposed preeclampsia experienced significantly higher rates of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes during their delivery admission compared to normotensive patients, with superimposed preeclampsia having the highest maternal mortality.
followup_time: Up to discharge from delivery admission
